title: Verify Events API setup
content_data:
This article introduces how to verify app data connection setup. The processes include: - Verify that events are received correctly. - Verify that events are configured and triggered correctly. # Verify that events are received correctly You can check if we have received your events under the app detail page. Click on your app's detail page and under the **Overview** tab, scroll down to the **Reporting** section: 1. Ensure **TikTok App Events API** is selected as **Data Source**. 2. Check the number of **Total Events**. Note that this count may be slightly delayed. # Verify that events are configured and triggered correctly through Test Events After you set up your app and are ready for reporting app events, you can send a test event to verify if everything works correctly. Make sure to remove `test_event_code` before switching to 'Production' mode. ## Steps 1. In Events Manager, click the app to view its configuration details. 2. In the **Test Events** tab, click the test code button in **Step 2** to copy the code.
3. In the body of your API request for reporting events, add a new field `test_event_code` and paste the code you get from Step 2 as the value of the field. Send the API request. Below is a test request example. You need to replace values for `Access-Token`, `event_source_id`, and `test_event_code` with your own. ```xcodeblock (code curl) curl --location --request POST 'https://business-api.tiktok.com/open_api/v1.3/event/track/' \ --header 'Access-Token: {{Access-Token}}' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "event_source": "app", "event_source_id": "{{TIKTOK_APP_ID}", "test_event_code": "{{YOUR_TEST_CODE}}", "data": [ { "event": "InstallApp", "event_time": 1684574395, "user": { "phone": "{{HASHED_PHONE}}", "email": "{{HASHED_EMAIL}}", "idfa": "{{IDFA}}", "idfv": "{{IDFV}}", "gaid": "{{GAID}}", "att_status": "AUTHORIZED" "locale": "en-US" }, "app": { "app_id": "com.test.flyingsneakers" "app_name": "Flying Sneakers" "app_version": "3.0.2" }, "ad": { "attributed": true, "callback": "{{CALLBACK}}", "campaign_id": "1700817380525057", "ad_id": "1700817380806706", "creative_id": "1700817378256945" "is_retargeting": false, "attribution_type": "click_through" }, "properties": { "contents": [ { "currency": "USD", "value": 200.0 "content_type": "product", { "price": 100.0, "quantity": 2, "content_id": "12345", "content_name": "Fancy-AirMax2.0 Black", "content_category": "Shoes - running shoes", "brand": "Fancy Sneakers" } ] } } ] }' (/code) ``` 4. Go to the **Test Events** tab of the app in **Events Manager**, and look for the test event in the **Event Activity** section. Any issues with the payload will show up to help you resolve the issues.
